newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia central bank details lending guidelines.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia central bank details lending guidelines.

text.p: Bank Negara Malaysia's new lending curbs for property and share purchases will include working capital requirements for stockbroking firms, banking industry sources said on Tuesday.

But it will exclude profit guarantees by merchant banks for companies seeking a stock exchange listing, the sources said, quoting from a new statement issued by Bank Negara to financial institutions detailing the guidelines.

In the statement to Malaysian banking institutions on Friday, Bank Negara detailed the categories that will and will not be exempt from its new lending curbs. The new measures have jolted the financial markets since the announcement on March 28.

Bank Negara had announced that lending to the property sector should not exceed 20 percent of a bank's outstanding loans. Loans for share purchases should not exceed 15 percent (30 percent for merchant banks) of total loans.

"The average monthly outstanding loans and advances extended to the broad property sector in any calender quarter shall not exceed 20 percent of the average monthly total outstanding loans in the previous quarter," the Bank Negara statement said.
Guarantees issued and property sector-related bonds and commercial paper purchased by banks are also subject to the same restrictions, but calculated separately.

Similarly, average monthly loans extended for purchase of shares and units of unit trust funds in any one quarter should not exceed 15 percent of an institution's average total loans in the previous quarter, the central bank said.
The rule also extends to guarantees, bonds and commercial papers. The limit is higher at 30 percent for merchant banks.
The Bank Negara statement said the quarter to June would be the first period of compliance for the institutions.

It said the curbs exempted houses costing less than 150,000 ringgit, office space for borrowers' own use, infrastructure projects like the new federal capital, Putra Jaya, and the Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC) and hotel construction.
The curbs would apply to working capital for investment and holding companies in the two sectors, financing mergers and acquisitions and buying shares under initial public offerings.
